messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

NOTE: Communications in your area are sometimes subject to routine monitoring by the authorities.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: If you were looking for a textbook picture of a regime approaching collapse, this is close to what you'd expect.
ATMOSPHERE: The mood has crossed a line — people are acting like the question isn't whether to act, but when.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] a well-placed source says the mood in the presidential palace is 'boring and orderly' — no crises being managed — the trend settling back toward normal
  - [Security Forces] a military court-martial was abruptly suspended, suggesting the chain of command can't enforce discipline (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Money And Logistics] This removes any serious doubt that past the point of concealment — informal money changers have raised their spread dramatically, pricing in a devaluation they expect
  - [Street Mood] women in the market are speaking openly about prices and blaming the government by name — a line they used to avoid (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Information Control] a pro-regime commentator went off-script on live television and wasn't cut off — the control room is distracted
  - [Personal Observations] contacts who tend to be alarmist have gone strangely calm, describing things as 'ugly but stable' — the trend settling back toward normal
  - [Diplomatic Signals] a friendly foreign intelligence contact said 'we're watching very carefully' — which is diplomat for alarm (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] the education ministry published its annual report on time with detailed performance metrics — the trend settling back toward normal

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If the economic deterioration is perceived by ordinary people as the regime's fault or as bad luck.
  - How deep the fractures go — surface-level dysfunction can mask either deeper rot or functioning parallel systems.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think we're seeing the regime's grip start to slip in ways that can't be easily hidden - the mood on the streets is shifting fast, and even the security forces seem to be losing their cohesion. It's still unclear how things will play out, but all signs point to a situation that's increasingly unstable and potentially nearing a tipping point.
